chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Barqī, from Saʿd ibn Saʿd al-Ashʿarī, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the prayer on Friday: how many rakʿahs is it before zawal? He said: six rakʿahs early in the morning, and six after that, making twelve rakʿahs, and six after that, making eighteen rakʿahs, and two rakʿahs after zawal, so these are twenty rakʿahs, and two rakʿahs after ʿasr, so these are twenty-two rakʿahs.

Also, if the earlier narrations have been reported permitting the advancement of the nawafil to the beginning of the day, then acting upon them is more appropriate and more virtuous, because a person is not secure from sudden death, so he may have hastened that in which there is reward and merit for him.

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: midday decline of the sun, marking the transition point for the prayer timing
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the prayer being discussed, specifically the Friday devotional prayer schedule
key_terms.النَّوَافِلِ: supererogatory prayers performed in addition to the obligatory prayers
key_terms.ثَوَابٌ: divine reward gained by performing the prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَاتٍ: units of prayer counted in the Friday nawafil
key_terms.صَدْرِ النَّهَارِ: the early part of the day, before the later prayer time
key_terms.فَضْلٌ: extra merit or virtue associated with the act
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, the day on which these nawafil are being described

ai.seo_question: How many nawafil are prayed on Friday, and is it permissible to perform them before zawal?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the number and scheduling of the nawafil on Friday, including their performance before zawal and after the obligatory times. It also states that advancing the nawafil to the early part of the day is preferable when narrations permit it, due to the uncertainty of death and the desirability of hastening toward reward.
